wrong_owner.title: Placement markers: audit the 55 hub-only-flagged waiting cards after f4caf04; re-place false positives to worker-2
wrong_owner.body:
Context (supervisor chat 20261111_090650_1247e7, 17:14Z): hub core f4caf041606 is live, and the 4-PR placement train t_01a1c8609d476871 is done. Even so, the worker-share watcher (`~/.hermes/bin/hermes-core-python -B ~/code/hermes-mods/plugins/coach/worker_share_watch.py --dry-run --json`) reports the hub at 8/7, starved, with worker-2 having 14 free slots and 69 cards waiting. Only 3-4 of those are spill-eligible. The rest are counted under: home gateway marker 38, local marker 17, uncarried requirement 6, assignee not allowlisted 4. Earlier sampling of titles and bodies suggested many of the home-gateway-marker flags are false positives (unverified).

## Do
1. For each waiting card flagged `home gateway marker` or `local marker`, record which marker text matched (from `kanban_placement` reason details) and decide whether the card truly needs hub-local state (hub logs, hub services, the hermes-hub checkout, MacBook/mini).
2. Move every false positive to `machine:worker-2` with `hermes kanban move --runs-on ... --reason`, and verify that each one is claimed.
3. If one marker pattern accounts for most of the false positives, fix that pattern in core `kanban_placement` with a test that fails before the change and passes after (core-dev skill; no checkout in ~/.hermes/hermes-agent).

## Acceptance
- A table of the 38 + 17 cards with columns: matched marker, verdict, action.
- `moved` events whose cards were then claimed on worker-2.
- If a pattern was fixed: the PR or commit plu

wrong_owner.title: BB mail E-06/E-01: prove Cloudflare always stamps its own Authentication-Results (forged verdict is trusted when it is absent and the sender writes no Received)
wrong_owner.body:
Found in review of t_01a1c9ad1ecbf51e (Worker E-06 owner-auth, landed ec400f1e0, Worker f67be637). Follow-up, not a regression: the acceptance of that card is met.

Observed (probe on landed ec400f1e0, `src/mail-auth.ts` `senderAuthenticated`; evidence `~/.hermes/kanban/evidence/t_01a1c9ad1ecbf51e/probe.mts` + `review-probe.log` on hermes-hub):
- Headers `[Cloudflare Received] [sender-written "Authentication-Results: mx.cloudflare.net; ... spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=you@example.com ..."] [From: you@example.com]` with NO upstream Received and NO Cloudflare-stamped Authentication-Results -> returns true (owner exception granted).
- With Cloudflare's own failing Authentication-Results present above it -> false. With an upstream Received above the forged header -> false.
So the "before the second Received" bound does not stop a direct-to-MX sender (the sender chooses whether to write a Received header). The only real protection is that Cloudflare Email Routing always stamps its own Authentication-Results first (or strips inbound ones claiming its authserv-id). That is unproven. The hub parser `hub/server/bbmail/parse.py` `_auth` has the same rule (senderVerified / owner attribution, E-01), where the impact is larger than the quota exception.

Do:
1. Measure, read-only, metadata only (no bodies, no addresses in output): across every message in the hub mailbox / parked R2 raw copies, count messages whose first Authentication-Results before the second Received is Cloudflare
